P1-01.title: Private report forms
P1-01.hint: Compare how your report is requested with how other student records are identified. Does the server check who owns the requested record?

P1-02.title: The forgotten console
P1-02.hint: A page missing from the navigation can still be reachable. Pay attention to the portal's operational features.

P1-03.title: Files on the lab box
P1-03.hint: Once inside the web container, practise listing directories and checking which files your account can read.

P2-01.title: The results backup
P2-01.hint: Inventory the lab's loopback services. An exposed backup deserves the same access checks as the main application.

P2-02.title: Internal trust
P2-02.hint: The public ports are only part of the network. Consider what a service inside the lab network assumes about its callers.

P3-01.title: The classmate search
P3-01.hint: Watch how the search responds to unusual input. Ask whether the input is treated strictly as data.

P3-02.title: The student review
P3-02.hint: A student's saved text may later be viewed by staff. Think about where that text is rendered and whose browser renders it.

P3-03.title: Who decides your role?
P3-03.hint: Inspect the browser's session state. Which values decide your identity and role, and what prevents someone from changing them?

P3-04.title: The marks ledger
P3-04.hint: Compare what the interface allows with what the marks endpoint actually checks. A hidden button is only a browser restriction.

P4-01.title: The server diagnostic
P4-01.hint: A diagnostic tool turns user input into a server action. Consider which interpreter receives that input.

P4-02.title: The uploaded asset
P4-02.hint: Follow an uploaded file through its whole lifecycle. The filename check and the way the server later uses the file may disagree.

P4-03.title: The remote school logo
P4-03.hint: When the portal imports a remote resource, the request starts on the server. Which destinations can that server reach?

P4-04.title: The fee receipt
P4-04.hint: Trace a payment from the browser to the ledger. Which amounts and approval decisions does the server calculate for itself?

P5-01.title: The browser configuration
P5-01.hint: Assets delivered to the browser are public to that browser's user. Review what the client is trusted to keep secret.

P5-02.title: Yesterday's configuration
P5-02.hint: The current tree is only one version of the project. Consider whether removing a value from a file removes its earlier copies.

P5-03.title: The dependency inventory
P5-03.hint: Compare pinned dependency versions with published advisories. The labctl audit command can help verify a real finding.

P5-04.title: The helpful error page
P5-04.hint: A failed request can reveal more than a successful one. Notice whether diagnostic details intended for developers reach the browser.

P5B-01.title: The legacy staff account
P5B-01.hint: Legacy authentication may store passwords differently. If you obtain a hash, examine its format and whether it uses a salt.

P5B-02.title: The sealed browser value
P5B-02.hint: Inspect the shape of the supposedly protected browser value. Reversible encoding and encryption provide different guarantees.

P5B-03.title: The signed API token
P5B-03.hint: A signature is only as strong as its secret. Examine the token format and think about how its signing key was chosen.

P5B-04.title: The encrypted transcript
P5B-04.hint: An encrypted value cannot remain secret if its decryption material is delivered alongside it. Review the browser assets.

P5B-05.title: The repeating blocks
P5B-05.hint: Compare repeated portions of the encrypted data. Some encryption modes preserve patterns between identical input blocks.

P5D-01.title: The saved preferences
P5D-01.hint: A browser preference should be plain data. Consider what happens when a server reconstructs an object supplied by the browser.

P5D-02.title: The class representative
P5D-02.hint: A settings form exposes a few fields. Does the server explicitly restrict which account properties a request may update?

P5D-03.title: The account recovery trail
P5D-03.hint: Account recovery creates temporary secrets. Check whether those secrets appear in diagnostic records that other users can reach.

SE-01.title: The staff noticeboard
SE-01.hint: The fictional staff member's public posts form a profile. Look for repeated personal details that might influence a weak password.

SE-02.title: The suspicious inbox
SE-02.hint: Compare the sender, destination links, and requested action in each sample message. Pressure is a clue, not proof on its own.

SE-03.title: The helpdesk conversation
SE-03.hint: Read the fictional staff directory and the scripted helpdesk's requirements. Small public facts may combine into a convincing identity claim.

F-01.title: The noticeboard
F-01.hint: The visible picture is only one part of an image file. Examine the information stored around its pixels.

F-02.title: The staff photo
F-02.hint: Compare the file's size with what its dimensions suggest. Is there more data than the image format needs?

F-03.title: The prize-giving photo
F-03.hint: The metadata is clean and no extra file is attached. Small changes within the pixels can carry information.

F-04.title: The school bell
F-04.hint: An animation is a sequence with timing information. Examine its individual frames rather than relying on playback.

F-05.title: The radio call
F-05.hint: The beeps have structure. Look for timing differences, pauses, and a code that can represent digits as well as letters.

F-06.title: The assembly recording
F-06.hint: Listening is only one way to examine sound. Try a visual representation of how its frequencies change over time.

F-07.title: The corridor CCTV
F-07.hint: Six seconds contains many separate images. Check whether ordinary-speed playback hides anything between them.
